<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /files/:fileId (route, a path literal in a comment in ObjectQL; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via valueSchemaFor (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FileRefusedValueSchema (symbol, a top-level const), /files/:fileId (route, a path literal in a comment in ObjectQL; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via /files/:fileId (route, a path literal in a comment in ObjectQL; a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via valueSchemaFor (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 31 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7146e07093e8f9fab686a6c8d5519d3968f00dc4` — the merge of head `4f460762974a6b438b8496ffcac99422cc4cccc6` into base `1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7146e07093e8f9fab686a6c8d5519d3968f00dc4 && git checkout 7146e07093e8f9fab686a6c8d5519d3968f00dc4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 4f460762974a6b438b8496ffcac99422cc4cccc6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04 && git merge --no-ff 4f460762974a6b438b8496ffcac99422cc4cccc6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1b99388505d33c940757e85685ca925d6cd57f04` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `faf689872c596d3170e2fe9913f2ccf90e5e84fe`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22593 (body, the Claim and the os-dev-report), PR #22620 (body, 16-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head), and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the ablation and the measured-on-main figures below are read off the dev's report, not reproduced.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Expanded accept set, the five `FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES` — RIGHT.** `valueSchemaFor(def, 'expanded')` widens from two members to three: `FileReferenceIdValueSchema | FileValueSchema | FileRefusedValueSchema`. The stored form is untouched and pinned (`field-value.test.ts`: the marker object is refused under the stored form). Multi-value fields carry the marker per element. ADR-0104 D1.2 names `expanded` as the read-time form the engine produces, and nothing decided there is reversed. Note, not owed for this landing: ADR-0104 §D3 prose still states the expanded form as `FileValueSchema` alone (it already tolerated the bare id without saying so); an erratum line there would keep the ADR grep-landing.
2. **`FileRefusedValueSchema` accept set — RIGHT.** Exactly `{ id: file-id token, metadataRefused: true }`, closed (`strictObject`, the file's third). Pinned: `metadataRefused: false` refused, a URL-shaped `id` refused, a missing `id` refused, an extra `name` refused with `unrecognized_keys`. Disjoint by shape from `FileValueSchema` (a `looseObject` whose `url` is required; the refused form has none), so a consumer tells the two object forms apart without a discriminator key.
3. **Served value, `ObjectQL.resolveFileReferences` — RIGHT.** On a thrown `PERMISSION_DENIED` from the caller-scoped `sys_file` sub-read, each id token in a file field becomes `{ id, metadataRefused: true }` (arrays per element; a non-token legacy URL string passes through), the record read still succeeds, and the arm logs `debug` instead of `warn`. The missing-table arm (silent, bare id) and every other failure (the existing `warn`, bare id) are unchanged and pinned, the `42501` database-ACL control included. This is the card's loud half, and the log level is AGENTS "Degradation log levels" third answer (the failure is delivered in the returned value, pinned in the seam's own test file as that section prescribes).
4. **Discriminator `isReadRefusal` — RIGHT.** Matches `error.code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` by literal. The spec declares the ADR-0112 vocabulary as literals (`api/errors.zod.ts`) and exports no per-code constant; twelve runtime source files already compare the same literal, so this is the repo's spelling, not a new dialect. `42501` is excluded on purpose and pinned. Declared limit, not a defect: a row-level short result on `sys_file` is not a throw and still reads as a bare id; that belongs to the access half (③ item 1).
5. **Public surface — RIGHT.** `FileRefusedValueSchema` (const) and `FileRefusedValue` (type) are added on `@objectstack/spec/data`; the five generated shards (`api-surface`, `authorable-surface`, `declaration-map`, `export-origins`, `json-schema.manifest`) and the two generated reference pages are regenerated, auto-gen headers intact, no hand edit; the ADR-0122 isomorphic pin moves 773 to 774 with no `Parsed` synonym (a literal and a lazy id schema, no default or transform); the strictness ledger gets its generated counts and one hand row. `authorable-surface` gains two keys for a shape that is served and never written; that is the generator's population (the sibling `FileValue` keys sit there under the same rule) and `Spec property liveness` is green on this head.
6. **Pins against the card — RIGHT.** (a) a reader without `sys_file` read sees the marker, on the seam (fake driver plus a refusing middleware) and on the real `SecurityPlugin` + `SqlDriver` stack, through `find` and `findOne`; (b) a record with no file still reads empty; (c) a reader with `sys_file` read gets the hydrated file; (d) the ablation (`if (isReadRefusal(error))` to `if (false && ...)`) turns the first pin red in both files (4 of 8, 1 of 4) with blob hashes before, after and restored, per the dev's report. The symptom was re-measured on `main` `d748ae80af` with the same two files before the change.
7. **Governance — RIGHT.** No governed surface on the file list, head repo equals base repo, 694 changed lines, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green. Not a Tier S landing; this record is owed by the `yes` declaration, not by a governed path.
8. **Hand-written docs — one understatement, carried to ③.** `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`, the `file` entry, states the expanded read form as "the media metadata object, whose only required member is `url`"; after this diff that is one form of three. The drift check named the page; the diff does not touch it.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec`: **minor — RIGHT.** Additive exports and a widened read union; nothing removed or renamed, so not breaking, and minor is the floor the `yes` declaration sets.
- `@objectstack/objectql`: **minor — RIGHT.** The served value gains a third form for a reader who used to get a bare id. On its own a fix (the card is `bug`, so `patch` would be the floor); the same declaration lifts it to minor. No removal and no rename, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed and none is present. The changeset body carries the FROM and TO and a consumer note, and names no tracker number and no model.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security`: a test file only, publishes nothing, no changeset owed — RIGHT.
- The `Clause-②` declaration reads `yes` with no arm on both carriers (PR body line 2 and the changeset); `yes` without an arm is a legal spelling (`(widening)` would be the fuller one), it matches a diff that widens an accept set and a public surface, and `Check Changeset` is green on this head. `skip-changeset` does not apply.

### ③ Boundary flags

The report carries `open_questions: []`; its declared deviations, limits and notes are each answered or escalated here.

1. **Access half (should `sys_file` metadata follow the parent record's read?) — ESCALATED to the owning seat.** Declared out by the card and left out by the diff (the file list has no plugin-security or service-storage source change). The report measured today's rule read-only: object-gate only on `sys_file`; `sys_attachment` rows follow the parent through `installAttachmentReadVisibility` but still behind an object grant; the download door derives from the owning or parent record and never asks `sys_file` read, so a member can be allowed the bytes and refused the name. The seat files the decision card for the maintainer; nothing for the dev.
2. **Cross-lane paths — OPEN for the seat before undraft.** `domain:spec` (`field-value.zod.ts`, its two pins, the five shards), `domain:services` (test only), `domain:devx` (two generated reference pages), plus the `docs/audits` ledger row. The Claim conditioned the spec path on need and promised re-declaration before the PR leaves draft; the need materialised (a served shape must be declared). The PR is still draft.
3. **Consumer relay (objectui at `12ff256`) — ESCALATED to the seat.** `readFileValue` already takes the marker through its object arm, so the console shows a non-empty generic "File" chip, never `EmptyValue`: refused and empty are already distinct at the consumer, which satisfies the card's "smallest shape that keeps the two states distinct". The restricted-state rendering (lock affordance, translated label, no thumbnail, keep the download affordance, the editable widget submits the bare id) is a relay to objectui, not this PR. Export is distinct too (`formatCsvCell` serialises the object).
4. **Merge of `origin/main` `d748ae80af` into the branch as the head — ANSWERED.** No conflicts, no `merge=os-regen` path routed; the head CI measured is that merge, and the later moves of `main` touch none of the diff's paths.
5. **First combined typecheck exit 1 (a concurrent rebuild in the same worktree), re-run alone exit 0 — ANSWERED by the check-runs.** `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace` and the aggregate `TypeScript Type Check` are all green on this head.
6. **Lint narrowed to the six changed TypeScript files, with the no-type-aware-linting invariance argument — ANSWERED by CI.** `Lint & Repo Gates` is the gate of record for the repo-wide lint and the `check:*` battery and is green on this head; the dev's 119 derived commands had all exited 0 locally.
7. **Row-level narrowing on `sys_file` still reads as a bare id — ANSWERED.** An existence probe is itself an access decision; it belongs to item 1.
8. **Noted, not filed (two) — ANSWERED as notes under Prime Directive #10.** The stale header comment in `attachment-access-hooks.ts` is comment drift; `plugin-approvals` `normalizeActionAttachment` would drop the marker but its only caller reads under the system context, so no refusal reaches it today. Non-blocking recommendation for the seat: a small follow-up card so `normalizeActionAttachment` carries the marker through, since it is a consumer of the expanded form the changeset's consumer note addresses.
9. **Hand-written docs — OWED, non-blocking for this verdict.** The `types.mdx` file entry (① item 8) needs one paragraph naming the refused read form; the PR already carries docs changes, so a rider before undraft is the cheapest carrier, a docs-only follow-up the alternative. The seat asks the dev.
10. **`Console Pin Gate` skipped — ANSWERED.** Path-filtered; the diff removes no export the pinned sibling imports, so no `.objectui-sha` bump is owed.

**Check-runs on this head, read 2026-10-10T06:20Z** — pending is recorded as pending, never as a pass. Green (27): Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate and shards 1/3, 2/3, 3/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core (5/6), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter. Pending (5): Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (6/6) — the `Test Core` required context is therefore not yet a pass on this head; the queue reads it, not this record.
